title: Bears board of directors votes to explore Indiana as priority location for new stadium
content:
The Chicago Bears board of directors voted Friday to further explore Hammond, Ind., as the priority location for the team’s next stadium. The vote comes less than a week after the spring session of the Illinois Legislature concluded with no solutions and no new legislation available for the Bears to proceed with a potential stadium project on the 326-acre property they own in suburban Arlington Heights, Ill.

For months, the Bears have vowed to complete an evaluation by late spring or early summer of two potential locations for a new stadium: Arlington Heights and Hammond.

In a joint statement Friday, Bears chairman George McCaskey and president and CEO Kevin Warren confirmed the team’s plan to advance its stadium development project in Indiana.

“We believe a world-class stadium project in Hammond will transform the region, connecting Northwest Indiana to the South Side of Chicago through the Loop and across neighborhoods and suburbs stretching north of the city,” they said. “It will bring Chicagoland together and deliver new opportunities to its residents and businesses.”

Friday’s development marks the first time the Bears’ board has cast a vote on the stadium situation, confirming the organization’s serious interest in a possible project in Indiana. Given the repeated stall-outs within Illinois in getting legislation passed that would help the team with tax certainty and infrastructure needs, Friday’s move shouldn’t register as a surprise.

The team’s intent now is to select a stadium site in Indiana and proceed further with its negotiations and planning within that state.

Friday’s declaration is not a “no turning back” moment in this prolonged saga. The Bears still face a heavy lift in working with local and state officials in Indiana to solidify a workable plan for a new stadium.

For an Indiana project to launch, the Bears still need ongoing environmental and traffic studies to be completed. The team is also working toward receiving concrete assurances on how the financial structure of any such stadium project would take shape, with the newly established Northwest Indiana Stadium Authority heavily involved.

By the same token, if Illinois officials are serious about keeping the team and confident a plan forward can materialize via legislation, they now face new pressure to accelerate their efforts to keep the Bears in the state.
